To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vitamin A and vitamin D are present in different concentrations in the six ILEs analyzed and that their content should be explicitly mentioned.
the content of vitamin A group and D2/D3 was variably present in the different ILEs, and that both should be mentioned in the products.
vitamin A and vitamin D contents in intravenous lipid emulsion are variable and should be explicitly mentioned on the product labels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of vitamins A and D in ILEs, which are not currently available.
the evaluation and quantification of vitamins A and D in six branded ILEs, which may have a potential clinical significance.
the potential intake of vitamins A and D through the use of ILEs in patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vitamin A group and the vitamin D2/D2 content in different ILE formulations are not negligible and should be taken into consideration when prescribing ILEs.
the presence of retinol and ergo- and chole-calciferol in different ILE is a matter of fact, but it should be explicitly mentioned on the products.

the content of vitamin A group is not clinically significant in the majority of ILEs, while it may be relevant in fish-oil based ones, and the vitamin D2/D 3 content is negligible in vegetable oil based ILEs and may be clinically significant in fish-oil ILEs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

vitamin D is present in ILE containing fish oils but not detectable in ILE containing vegetable oil, whereas vitamin A is present in IEL containing vegetable oils and in those containing fish oils, but not detectable for the latter.
the content of vitamins A and D in the ILE should be reported on the label, and their clinical relevance should be evaluated.
vitamin A and vitamin D are present in the ILE formulations, but their amounts are not sufficient to be considered as a nutritional supplement for patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of vitamin A and D in ILEs is clinically relevant.
the vitamin A group and D2/D3 contents of different ILEs should be reported to allow the clinician to make a more rational choice of ILE for patients with vitamin deficiency.
the presence of vitamins A and D in ILEs may be relevant for patients receiving parenteral nutrition for prolonged periods.
